name: file.delete
description: Delete a file or empty directory. Hard delete — bypasses Recycle Bin / Trash. Pass `recursive: true` to remove non-empty directories.

recursive.description: If path is a directory, delete its contents recursively. Without this flag, deleting a non-empty directory returns ERR not_empty.

deleted.description: True when the path was deleted. False is reserved for future soft-delete semantics; today the response is always true on success (errors raised otherwise).

x-implementations.name: delete_file_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `DeleteFileW` for files. Returns ERR permission_denied for read-only files (caller must clear FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY first via a future file.set_attributes verb).

x-implementations.name: remove_directory_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RemoveDirectoryW` for empty directories. With `recursive: true`, the agent walks the tree first via FindFirstFile/FindNextFile + DeleteFile, then RemoveDirectory.

windows-modern.description: DeleteFileW for files, RemoveDirectoryW for directories. Hard delete — does not route through the Recycle Bin (SHFileOperation is intentionally NOT used). Reparse points are removed without traversal — `recursive: true` removes the link, not the link target.

windows-classic.description: DeleteFileA / DeleteFileW depending on NT version, plus RemoveDirectory. Same hard-delete behaviour — Recycle Bin requires SHFileOperation, which the agent intentionally does not use. Pre-NT-5 has no reparse points; recursive delete behaves uniformly.
